state.orbifold_chi: chi = 1 - (1/p + 1/q + 1/r) > 0 for all p, q, r >= 3
state.covering: Darmon-Granville finite abelian cover to genus g >= 2 curve
state.effective_height: Baker-Wustholz linear forms in logarithms combined with nu_p(Delta) >= 18

baker_wustholz_effectiveness.instructions: Can effective linear forms in logarithms (Baker-Wustholz) provide an explicit upper bound B_0 on bases for fixed hyperbolic signatures (p, q, r)?

criteria.true: Explicit height bounds exist for fixed signatures via S-unit equations and linear forms in logarithms
criteria.false: Baker-Wustholz cannot bound bases without unproved ABC or Vojta conjectures

darmon_granville_fidelity.instructions: Does the Darmon-Granville 1995 covering theorem rigorously map primitive Beal solutions of signature (p, q, r) with 1/p+1/q+1/r < 1 to rational points on a curve of genus g >= 2?

criteria.true: Darmon-Granville unconditionally constructs a genus g >= 2 covering curve over a number field
criteria.false: The covering construction requires special hypotheses not satisfied by Beal triples

residual_signature_risk.instructions: Which open residual signature represents the greatest arithmetic risk for primitive solutions below search bounds?

criteria.3_4_7: Signature (3, 4, 7) has smallest total exponent sum among ternary hyperbolic open cases
criteria.3_5_7: Signature (3, 5, 7) has genus-0 subvarieties in modular Jacobian
criteria.4_4_7: Signature (4, 4, 7) has equal exponents 4,4 allowing elliptic curve Frey descent
criteria.none: All open signatures have chi >= 1/12 and are strictly hyperbolic with finite rational points
